items.name: LiveKit client behind VoiceTransport, zero vendor-type leakage

LiveKitVoiceTransportVendorLeakageTest (reflection-based) asserts zero io.livekit.* types on public API surface. ./gradlew :voice:testDebugUnitTest -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 15/15 passed.

items.name: Full spoken round-trip via emulator injectAudio/streamAudio, RMS above silence threshold
items.blocker: This host has no /dev/kvm device (confirmed via `ls /dev/kvm` -> 'No such file or directory' at session start), so the Android emulator cannot enable KVM-based hardware acceleration and cannot boot at all on this machine, with or without -no-window. Without a booted emulator there is no gRPC endpoint to call injectAudio (inject synthetic audio in) or streamAudio (capture synthetic TTS out) against, so this item cannot be executed in this environment as-is. This is the same root-cause hardware limitation independently confirmed by lane 1.1 on this identical host.

items.name: Barge-in interrupts TTS mid-sentence (V1/V2/V3)
items.evidence: Split verdict, resolved after initial review flagged untested plumbing: LiveKitVoiceTransportBargeInTest (new, 2/2 passing, part of :voice:testDebugUnitTest now 17/17) directly unit-tests both directions of barge-in against a fake LiveKitRoomClient - (a) send(VoiceEvent.BargeIn) invokes roomClient.signalBargeIn() exactly once and does not fall through to publishAudio, and (b) a room-level RoomEvent.BargeInDetected surfaces as VoiceEvent.BargeIn on incomingEvents. Also replaced the original placeholder implementation (which signalled barge-in by publishing zero-length/silent audio - not a real interrupt signal) with a dedicated LiveKitRoomClient.signalBargeIn() method, so the code path is both correctly designed and now verified, not just present. Live behavioral confirmation (TTS audibly stops mid-sentence on-device) remains BLOCKED-no-dev-kvm - no emulator/device available in this session - and the consumer that would react to signalBargeIn() server-side lives in voice-worker/ (in-lane) plus any app-level playback code outside this lane's ownership, so full E2E stop-of-audio was not exercised end-to-end.

items.name: PTT (push-to-talk) mode toggles and works as fallback (V6)
items.evidence: android/voice/ PttController: OFF/ARMED/TRANSMITTING state machine, fully unit tested without emulator or LiveKit. 8/8 PttController tests passing (part of :voice:testDebugUnitTest 15/15).

items.name: Distinct earcon per state (listening/thinking/speaking) + FGS notification update (V7/V8)
items.evidence: EarconMapper/EarconStateDriver (state -> earcon mapping) and VoiceServiceStateReducer (TransportState x substate -> notification text + earcon) both unit tested in isolation: 11/11 reducer/earcon tests passing, plus ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 7/7 passed. VoiceForegroundService wraps the reducer's output against real NotificationManager/EarconPlayer.
items.blocker: The remaining part of this item -- confirming earcons are audibly heard through a device audio output and that the real Android NotificationManager visibly renders/updates the foreground-service notification as state transitions occur -- requires a running Android device or emulator; plain JVM unit tests execute outside the Android framework and cannot exercise real NotificationManager rendering or AudioTrack playback. This host has no /dev/kvm device (confirmed at session start via `ls /dev/kvm` -> 'No such file or directory'), so the Android emulator cannot boot, and no physical Android device is attached to this headless machine. There is no non-device path to observe real notification/audio behavior.
